already-have.reason: Not implemented, but NOT novel: CS-10 is a re-statement and widening of an already-recorded, owner-accepted ADR roadmap item. docs/erc7730-root-rotation-and-update-policy.md:103-122 ("Roadmapped (NOT v1): a C10-signed descriptor-root artifact", PQDESC_V1) already designs a C10-signed, monotonic-versioned, flash-page-stored root with compiled-in fallback, and explicitly DEFERS it "until the release-cadence pain is real". docs/security/vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:147-150 and :700-708 later re-raised it as an open checklist item ("Build the PQDESC_V1 signed-descriptor-root channel ... highest leverage item in either round") and :625-628 says it has no freeze coupling and "can proceed immediately". So the direction is endorsed in-repo, the code does not exist (roots are compiled-in statics, no catalogue CMD), and no GitHub issue tracks building it. It is therefore a live, untracked, deferred item - refuted=false. However, two parts of CS-10 as written contradict the recorded design (a separate vendor catalogue key; a flash-page floor instead of an OTP-anchored one) and it understates scope (four roots + Bloom + P73K/P73S, not one root). Priority stays P2 at most and realistically post-v1: ADR decision 2 says no separate descriptor-update path ships in v1, the whole release chain (PQFW_V1) is quarantined, and ERC-8176 provenance (#377) is a P0 ship-blocker that gates any production root at all.
already-have.corrections: 1) Re-frame as "implement the already-designed, deferred PQDESC_V1 channel (ADR 2026-07-02) and extend it from the descriptor root to the whole catalogue", not as a new Trezor-parity idea. Cite docs/erc7730-root-rotation-and-update-policy.md:103-122 and docs/security/vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:147-150,700-708 as the owning docs; amend those rather than creating a new design doc. 2) KEY: the ADR says the artifact is signed "with the SAME C10 release key that authenticates firmware (invariant #5 - one signature primitive; no new key, no classical signer)" (policy doc :110-112) and "must reuse the C10 release key, never introduce a second signer" (:229-231). CS-10's "vendor catalogue key whose pubkey is pinned in the secure image" is a second key = conflict. If a separate key is wanted, the only new argument available is the unfrozen per-vendor-key C10 signature cap (OPEN-C10-1, #225) - frequent catalogue signatures spend the few-time budget of the firmware key; that must be put to the owner as an explicit decision, not assumed. 3) FLOOR: ADR specifies root_version monotonic "OTP-anchored, like the FW rollback floor" (:113-115); CS-10 puts the floor in a config flash page. The proposal's own risk note (do not reuse the rejected unary tally) is correct, but the floor design must be reconciled with the Draft 1.1/1.2 typed-floor work (#540, #224) rather than invented separately. 4) SCOPE understated: the catalogue is not five 32-byte values. The known-call Bloom is 16 KiB of included bytes (secure/src/db_roots.rs:136-142, include_bytes!), plus the P73K refused-known set F and the 256-byte P73S receipt, all co-embedded in the signed secure image (policy doc decision 3, :41-73). A "Bloom hash" in the bundle means the Bloom + P73K bytes must also be delivered and durably stored - multiple flash pages, not one config page - and the companion pairing model (#379) which today authenticates P73S via the signed secure-image hash must be redesigned for a root that is no longer image-bound. 5) AUTHORITY: policy doc step 6 (:195-203) says every contract-call C->F movement "expands signing authority when erc7730-forced-blind is enabled and therefore needs an explicit owner decision; catalogue churn cannot silently approve it". A field catalogue update moves C/F without a firmware release, so CS-10 must either exclude F/P73K/Bloom from the data channel (C-only additions) or carry that owner gate; it also interacts with the unfrozen forced-blind v2 design (#329). 6) Leaf type-domain byte: today each DB has its own pinned root and the same sha256(0x00||leaf) leaf prefix (tx/src/erc20/merkle.rs:47, pqsigner-erc7730/src/bundle.rs:21, dbgen/src/merkle.rs:149); cross-type confusion is prevented by separate roots, which CS-10 keeps (bundle lists four distinct roots), so the type byte is only needed if roots are merged - optional, and changing leaf hashing rotates every root. 7) The "blank page -> compiled-in fallback" must be "stored root used only if present AND newer than the image's" (ADR :115-116) plus FI-hardening of the root-select branch, otherwise a firmware update that ships a newer catalogue is shadowed by a stale page. 8) Sequencing: blocked behind #377 (no production-authorised root exists at all; catalogue is dev-unattested) and the PQFW_V1 release quarantine; a data channel verified by a quarantined verifier/key inherits no production authority. 9) repo_evidence fix: the proto grep claim is literally false (DESCRIPTOR matches at proto/src/lib.rs:1280,1292,1319,1341,1362,1990), though the substantive claim (no catalogue/root-update CMD) is true; cost L is plausible only for descriptor-root-only, the full-catalogue version is XL.

feasible.reason:
CS-10 does address the stated staleness threat and needs no board change, but as written it is under-specified, contradicts an accepted ADR on three points, and is a near-duplicate of an already roadmapped and deferred design. Not refuted; it needs heavy correction before it is usable.

**The code premise is true.** All catalogue roots are compiled in (/home/nicola/repos/PQSigner_OS/secure/src/db_roots.rs:59-142) and proto has no catalogue command. A C10 verifier and a pinned vendor key already exist in the secure image (secure/src/fw_update/vendor_pubkey.rs:1-33), so S-world verification of a 4008-byte signature is feasible.

**It is not novel.** docs/erc7730-root-rotation-and-update-policy.md:107-124 already roadmaps a "C10-signed descriptor-root artifact" (PQDESC_V1) and defers it "until the release-cadence pain is real". CS-10's repo_evidence does not cite this ADR.

**Soundness holes and bypasses:**

1. **A root is not the whole catalogue.** The proposal stores four roots plus a Bloom *hash*, but the firmware consumes more than that at sign time:
   - `ERC7730_DESCRIPTOR_COUNT` is a compile-time const used for canonical-index enforcement (secure/src/tx/erc7730.rs:53-75).
   - The known-calls Bloom is 16 KiB of data, not a hash (pqsigner-erc7730/src/known_calls.rs:21; consumed at secure/src/tx/erc7730.rs:233-520 and secure/src/tx/display/safe_display.rs:195,219).
   - The refused-known set P73K is a 33,336-byte in-image static (db_roots.rs:147-153).
   - An 8 KiB page cannot hold the Bloom (2 pages) or P73K (5 pages).
   - If only the root rotates, the in-image K/F artifacts no longer satisfy the generation-time proofs C ∩ F = ∅ and C ∪ F = K (ADR decision #3, lines 46-74).
   - With `erc7730-forced-blind` on, a tuple whose descriptor the new root drops but which is still in the in-image F can reach the forced-blind ceremony; a tuple dropped from K falls to the generic blind ladder.
   - The catalogue signer therefore gains clear-to-blind downgrade authority that today requires an owner-reviewed firmware release (ADR step 6, lines 205-211). A monotonic data_version does not stop this.

2. **Provenance fences become moot.** The compile-time fences that reject a dev-unattested catalogue under `mode-production` (db_roots.rs:248-257) bind only the compiled-in root. A runtime root bypasses them unless the bundle carries a provenance field that is enforced at runtime.

3. **Invariant #10 visibility regresses.** The boot fingerprint measures the firmware slots only. A page-stored root changes what the device renders as "clear" with no change to the 8 words. The one-time bundle-fingerprint confirm happens on a possibly attacker-driven companion session, and nothing is shown afterwards at boot or sign time.

4. **A separate "vendor catalogue key" weakens the trust base.** Compromise of that one key, plus a companion that prompts the PIN-unlocked user to confirm, yields attacker-chosen descriptors, token decimals/symbols and names. That is a WYSIWYS break without touching the firmware key.

5. **The flash floor can be erased.** The proposal falls back to the compiled-in root when the page is blank, so the floor is only as strong as the page's survival and the image-carried minimum. The ADR requires an OTP-anchored monotonic counter. I did not trace whether wipe or duress paths would erase a new page.

6. **A power-cut during the page rewrite is unspecified.** Erase-then-program on a single page leaves it blank, which silently falls back to the older compiled-in root. It needs a two-copy or journaled commit.

**Feasibility:**

- No pin or board change is needed. Kind stays mixed (firmware plus key-custody and release process); it is not hardware.
- There is no free flash page. The frozen registry assigns all 256 pages exactly once (geometry/src/lib.rs:121-138). The only spare is bank-2 page 127, `ReservedErased`, which "must remain erased" (lines 106, 137).
- A "dedicated config page" therefore needs a geometry-registry change (which the proposal does not flag), in practice carving it from a slot:
  - The secure slot has 34,071 bytes of headroom without ui-px and is 76,949 bytes over with it.
  - The new page must be added to `updater_must_preserve` (geometry/src/lib.rs:186-199).
  - It needs a policy in the first-boot blank-check loop, which hardcodes pages 123..=127 (secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:197-202).
feasible.corrections:
**Design corrections**

1. Re-base on the existing ADR roadmap item (docs/erc7730-root-rotation-and-update-policy.md:107-124, 229-232) rather than presenting a new design. Reuse the same C10 release key with a domain tag; do not add a new catalogue key. Anchor the floor in OTP, which depends on the unapproved Draft 1.1 typed-floor API. Do not use a flash-page floor.

2. Version the catalogue as one atomic unit: root, leaf count, 16 KiB Bloom, P73K F-set, P73S receipt, IR/compiler schema version, provenance class and minimum firmware version. Then pick one of:
   - store Bloom and P73K on-device, which needs about 8 pages rather than 1; or
   - restrict runtime refresh to additive-only changes that provably leave K and F unchanged (ERC-20 and names roots are the easy first slice); or
   - have the companion supply the Bloom per sign, hashed against a stored hash (16 KiB per request).

   Removing a tuple from C or K must still require a firmware release.

3. Enforce provenance at runtime. A dev-unattested bundle must be refused under `mode-production`, mirroring db_roots.rs:248-257.

4. Flag the geometry change explicitly. No free page exists, the registry is frozen and CI-pinned, and `updater_must_preserve` plus the first-boot blank check (secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:197-202) must be amended. Specify a power-cut-safe two-copy commit.

5. Restore invariant-#10 visibility: show the installed catalogue data_version and fingerprint on a boot or sign-time trusted screen.

6. The proposal does not address the ERC-8176 brittleness it cites in its threat statement. Host-side attestation is still needed per catalogue; only the delivery vehicle changes.

**Trezor precedent errors** (checked in /home/nicola/repos/trezor-firmware)

- Trezor has no stored, monotonic on-device floor. `MIN_DATA_VERSION_V1/V2` are build-time timestamps compiled into each firmware (core/embed/rust/src/definitions/generated.rs:6-8, constants.rs:26-29). blob.rs:50-54 only rejects a blob older than that constant.
- Trezor is stateless. Each definition is host-supplied per request with its own Merkle proof and CoSi signature (blob.rs:33-89); nothing is persisted and there is no update command or confirm ceremony. CS-10's persisted-root model is a different, higher-risk architecture, so "novelty: parity" is wrong.
- "One-month freshness floor" is misread. docs/common/external-definitions.md:38 says the floor timestamp is typically one month before firmware release; it is not a rolling freshness window. The cited lines 60-66 are the token URL section, not the floor.
- Built-ins override externals in Trezor (core/src/apps/ethereum/definitions.py:38-47, 73-80; the cited lines are approximately right). CS-10 inverts this: the page root overrides the compiled-in root.
- Type byte, Merkle and the CoSi threshold of 1 for format v2 are accurate (external-definitions.md, format section; blob.rs:45-48).

**Calibration**

- Priority P2 → P3: explicitly deferred by ADR, no devices shipped, and the fail-closed policy makes a stale catalogue inconvenient, not unsafe.
- Cost L → XL: geometry change, multi-page atomic catalogue store, new signed-artifact parser with Kani and adversarial review, runtime count/Bloom/P73K/provenance plumbing, OTP-floor dependency, release and companion tooling.
- Kind: mixed (firmware plus release/key process). No hardware.
